title: The Ratio Ceiling: Why a Full Waitlist Doesn't Mean a Fully Earning Childcare Centre
linkedin:
Term 4 waitlists at childcare centres across the East Coast are stretching months past what any single intake could fill.

Most directors read that as the clearest sign their business is healthy. It usually isn't the number that matters most.

Revenue in a childcare centre is set by the roster, not the enrolment list. Every room operates under a maximum educator-to-child ratio, and if there aren't enough qualified, rostered educators on a given day, that room runs under its licensed number regardless of how many families are waiting.

The enrolment pipeline and the billable place are two different things. The gap between them is where a meaningful share of expected revenue quietly disappears, and it rarely shows up as a clean line on a monthly report.

This isn't a story about any one centre getting something wrong. It's the pattern the whole sector is working through right now, shaped by a tight educator labour market rather than any individual's planning.

Fixed costs like rent and compliance overheads don't shrink when a room runs under capacity. The business absorbs that gap entirely through margin, often without anyone naming it as its own line item.

The directors tracking staffed capacity separately from enrolled capacity are making very different staffing and pricing decisions right now, just as 2027 enrolments lock in.

If you run a childcare centre on Queensland's East Coast, in New South Wales, or in Victoria, you're probably taking enrolments for 2027 right now, and the waitlist might be the longest it's been all year.

Here's something worth checking before you read that waitlist as good news on its own. Revenue in a childcare centre is actually decided by the roster, not the enrolment list. Every room has a maximum ratio of educators to children, and if there aren't enough qualified staff rostered on a given day, that room runs below its licensed number no matter how many families are waiting for a place.

This is the pattern a lot of centres are working through at the moment, driven by how tight the educator labour market has become. The cost side doesn't move with it either. Rent, insurance and compliance overheads stay the same whether a room is full or short a shift, so the gap shows up in margin rather than in any single number on a monthly report.

If you haven't separated your licensed capacity from your actually staffed capacity this term, it's worth doing before next year's enrolments are fully locked in.
